attributes.title: Preregistration: Block IV Adaptive Agency and Structural Generalisation - Theory of Everything Research Programme.
attributes.description:
This preregistration freezes the first confirmatory study for Experimental Block IV of the Theory of Everything Research Programme. 

Block IV tests whether artificial agents can adapt to previously unseen causal structures, compositions and problem families, and whether explicit predictive modelling and counterfactual rollout make selective causal contributions beyond serious model-free and heuristic alternatives. Seven hypotheses (H4.1-H4.7), twenty held-out seeds, confirmatory-only structural task variants, architecture classes, compute/storage matching rules, model-corruption and correction interventions, primary estimands, thresholds and Retain/Restrict/Reduce/Suspend/Reject rules are frozen before confirmatory execution. Development-only simulations were used to validate the implementation and choose prospective thresholds; their outcomes are disclosed and excluded from confirmatory evidence. 

No Block IV confirmatory seed had been executed when the protocol was frozen. A positive result would support only scoped causal contributions to structural generalisation in the registered artificial environments. It would not establish general intelligence, universal necessity of world models, reflective self-awareness or phenomenal consciousness. 

Related methodological framework: Craggs, K. (2026), Testing a Candidate Dependency Architecture: An Adversarial Experimental Programme for Maintenance, Heredity, Learning, Agency and Self-Modelling, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.22857230.
tags: Theory of Everything Research Programme adaptive agency structural generalisation world models predictive modelling counterfactual rollout causal intervention model-based control model-free control causal reversal compositional generalisation delayed consequences preregistration reproducibility open science

344-2.value:
This study asks whether structural generalisation differs from ordinary interpolation, and whether explicit predictive modelling and counterfactual rollout make selective causal contributions when familiar causal relations, compositions or problem families change.

H4.1: Model-based architectures adapt selectively faster when familiar causal relations are altered.

H4.2: Counterfactual rollout contributes specifically when alternative delayed futures must be compared.

H4.3: Explicit model-based control provides structural-generalisation benefits beyond a serious compute- and storage-matched model-free alternative.

H4.4: Task-relevant internal world-model content is causally used during planning.

H4.5: Correcting a corrupted internal model selectively restores the corresponding planning capability.

H4.6: Structural generalisation extends beyond ordinary interpolation and parameter variation.

H4.7: The cross-task structural-generalisation profile is not reducible to one preregistered simple heuristic.

Each hypothesis has a separate preregistered decision rule. Successful model-free or heuristic bypasses count against necessity even if the model-based mechanism remains causally useful.

344-4.value: Data does not yet exist. No part of the data that will be used for this analysis plan exists, and no part will be generated until after this plan is registered.

344-14.value: Development-only simulations exist and were used to debug the implementation, harden controls and choose prospective thresholds. Those development task variants and seeds are excluded from confirmatory evidence. The exact confirmatory structural variants use held-out context counts, offsets, reward schedules, component counts and problem-family parameters that have not been executed. Twenty new confirmatory seeds are frozen in advance. Seven machine-readable manifests and their referenced configurations are SHA-256 locked, and the execution registry refuses confirmatory execution until a public preregistration is recorded.

value: Simulation study: Using existing or synthetic data to assess performance of a model, mimic operation of an existing or proposed system, or predict possible outcomes in a controlled context. This may include demonstration of methods, many varieties of modeling, prediction of policy impacts, simulating behavior or outcomes in a population, and other designs.

Direct inference on causal relationship(s): This study is intended to infer or estimate a causal relationship between two or more variables. It is designed specifically for the purposes of causal inference or identification.

344-38.value: The study does not involve human participants. Protection against analyst flexibility is provided by confirmatory-only task variants, held-out seeds, frozen machine-readable manifests, locked decision rules, a preregistration execution gate and automated analysis. Development variants are separated from decisive evaluation variants.

344-40.value: The investigation is a controlled computational experiment using transparent low-dimensional graph/control tasks. Architecture classes include reactive control, history-sensitive model-free control, predictive modelling without rollout, model-based rollout control and a serious compute/storage-matched model-free bypass. Separate task families test causal reversal, delayed consequences, novel composition and withheld problem-family structure. Targeted model corruption and correction supply intervention-rescue tests. Each condition is repeated across twenty independently registered seeds. Adaptation time and final performance are analysed separately.

344-44.value: Random seeds determine held-out surface permutations, action assignments and task-specific structural realisations. The exact twenty seeds are fixed before execution in BLOCK4_CONFIRMATORY_SEEDS_V1.txt; they are not generated adaptively during the confirmatory study.

344-47.value: Data will be generated by executing the seven frozen Block IV manifests after the OSF registration becomes public. Each run records the registered seed identity, architecture, task-family condition, intervention condition and primary outcome, together with provenance hashes and runtime metadata. No confirmatory task or seed will be executed before the preregistration gate is opened.

344-51.value: The confirmatory unit is the independently initialised seed/replicate. Twenty seeds are used for each preregistered hypothesis. Within a seed, multiple architecture or intervention conditions are paired where defined. Individual decision steps within a run are not treated as independent confirmatory replicates.

344-53.value: Twenty independent seeds provide a consistent replicate count with the later Block I and Blocks II-III confirmatory studies while permitting strong seed-consistency criteria such as 18/20 paired successes. The sample size was fixed after development but before any confirmatory execution and is not responsive to interim outcomes.

344-55.value: Confirmatory data collection begins only after the OSF preregistration is public and the execution registry is formally unlocked. All twenty registered seeds will be run for every frozen manifest unless a run is invalid under a preregistered technical invalidity condition. Scientific failure is not a stopping rule. Data collection ends after the complete seven-manifest, twenty-seed protocol has been executed and provenance validated.

344-58.value: Manipulated variables include architecture class; presence or absence of multi-step rollout; causal-rule reversal; structural novelty class; planning horizon; targeted versus irrelevant model corruption; model correction; and heuristic/model-free bypass architecture. The exact levels are specified in the attached frozen manifests and environment configurations.

344-62.value: Primary measurements include adaptation interactions, final success/accuracy, success by novelty class, structural-generalisation gap by class, A3-A2 rollout-ablation effect, planning-horizon profile, A3-A4PLUS success difference, counted inference operations, storage slots, targeted model-corruption effect, model-correction rescue effect and cross-family heuristic success.

344-66.value: No universal intelligence or structural-generalisation score is constructed. Derived quantities are hypothesis-specific: paired adaptation-time difference; architecture success difference; corruption effect = intact success minus corrupted success; rescue effect = corrected success minus corrupted success; and class-specific structural-generalisation gap = ordinary held-out performance minus performance under the nominated structural class. Adaptation time and final performance remain separate.

344-71.value: Primary inference is threshold-based according to the frozen decision rules. Seed-level paired contrasts are aggregated across the twenty independent replicates. Architecture-by-novelty profiles are reported separately by class. Descriptive uncertainty intervals may accompany the estimates but do not replace the preregistered thresholds. No individual within-run decision step is treated as an independent replicate.

344-75.value: Binary success is coded 0/1. Adaptation time is recorded as the number of post-change interactions required to reach the preregistered accuracy criterion. No outcome-dependent transformations or recodings are planned.

344-77.value: H4.1-H4.7 use the exact numerical Retain/Restrict/Reduce/Suspend/Reject rules embedded in their frozen manifests. No null-hypothesis p-value threshold is the primary decision criterion. Because the decisive contrasts are separately preregistered for different hypotheses and task families, no post-hoc selection of favourable comparisons is permitted. Family-specific bypass successes are reported even when they narrow a positive model-based result.

344-79.value: All valid registered seed runs are included. A run may be excluded only for preregistered technical invalidity such as manifest-validation failure, environment-execution failure or unverifiable provenance. Poor performance, failure to adapt or defeat by a bypass is scientific evidence and is not an exclusion criterion. No statistical outlier removal is planned.

344-81.value: The simulation is designed to produce complete deterministic-format output for each registered run. Missing output caused by a technical failure is treated as an invalid run and rerun only under the identical frozen manifest and seed, with the failed attempt preserved in the audit trail. Scientific non-success is recorded as an outcome, not as missing data.

344-83.value: Secondary reporting includes task-specific heuristic successes, compute/storage matching diagnostics, per-class generalisation profiles and descriptive uncertainty. Any analysis not specified in the frozen record will be labelled exploratory and will not alter the preregistered decisions.

344-86.value: Block IV follows completed confirmatory work on maintenance, reproduction/heredity/selection, and retention/feedback/learning. Those earlier results do not imply structural generalisation or intelligence. Block IV is deliberately independent in its evidential claim: it tests whether explicit predictive structure and rollout are causally useful under held-out structural novelty while allowing serious non-model alternatives to succeed.
